Let \(p=2027\), so \(n=\frac{p-1}{2}=1013\). Work modulo \(p\).

For \(0\le k\le p-1\), set
\[
a_k=\binom{2k}{k}2^k.
\]

By Lucas’s theorem, if \(k>n\), then \(2k=p+r\) with \(0\le r<p\) and \(r<k\), so
\[
\binom{2k}{k}\equiv \binom{1}{0}\binom{r}{k}=0 \pmod p.
\]
Thus only \(0\le k\le n\) contribute.

For \(0\le k\le n\),
\[
\binom{n}{k}
=\frac{1}{k!}\prod_{j=0}^{k-1}\frac{p-1-2j}{2}
\equiv (-1)^k\frac{1\cdot3\cdots(2k-1)}{2^k k!}
= (-4)^{-k}\binom{2k}{k}.
\]
Hence
\[
\binom{2k}{k}2^k \equiv (-8)^k\binom{n}{k}\pmod p.
\]

Therefore
\[
S\equiv \sum_{k=0}^n k\binom{n}{k}(-8)^k.
\]
This is the derivative at \(x=1\) of \((1-8x)^n\):
\[
S\equiv \left.\frac{d}{dx}(1-8x)^n\right|_{x=1}
= -8n(1-8)^{n-1}
= -8n(-7)^{1012}.
\]
Since \(8n=8104\equiv -4\pmod{2027}\), we get
\[
S\equiv 4(-7)^{1012}\pmod{2027}.
\]

Now
\[
\left(\frac{-7}{2027}\right)
=
\left(\frac{-1}{2027}\right)\left(\frac{7}{2027}\right)
= (-1)\bigl(-\left(\frac{2027}{7}\right)\bigr)=1,
\]
because \(2027\equiv 4\pmod 7\) and \(4\) is a square mod \(7\). Thus by Euler’s criterion,
\[
(-7)^{1013}\equiv 1 \pmod{2027},
\]
so
\[
(-7)^{1012}\equiv (-7)^{-1}\pmod{2027}.
\]
Since \(-7\cdot 579\equiv 1\pmod{2027}\),
\[
S\equiv 4\cdot 579=2316\equiv 289\pmod{2027}.
\]

\[
\boxed{289}
\]
